sn46.56:1.5: In [dn2](), Pūraṇa Kassapa posits the view that there are no results of deeds, while Makkhali argues that there is no cause for the purification of beings. The exact view stated here does not appear elsewhere in the Pali canon, but does not contradict Pūraṇa’s other views. If action has no consequence, then there is nothing we can do to gain wisdom. This view also explains why his own students did not respect his understanding ([mn77:6.22]()). Nonetheless, he claimed to be omniscient ([an9.38:2.1]()), presumably without cause.
